item.title: Veterans Day 2026 brings free meals at popular restaurants — and some deals don't end Nov. 11
item.description: About 30 restaurants are offering Veterans Day deals on Nov. 11, from Outback Steakhouse's free Bloomin' Onion to Buffalo Wild Wings' boneless wings.
item.content:encoded:
Veterans and active-duty military members can find free food and other promotions at restaurants across the country on Veterans Day, Nov. 11. Some offers also give customers a reason to return for another deal later.

About 30 restaurant brands are included in Dinova's 2026 Veterans Day Dining Guide, according to Alison Quinn, the company's Florida-based president. 

The guide is in its fifth year and includes national and regional chains like Bonefish Grill, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Hooters, Outback Steakhouse and Red Lobster.

102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115'

"What we're starting to see now is it's going beyond Veterans Day, to try to give back to the vets in a way that is more meaningful," Quinn told Fox News Digital. "Just not about one day but come back and we'll give you something again."

Quinn pointed to California-based Hoffman Hospitality Group, which is offering select meals to veterans and a $10 bonus card for a future visit. Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que is among the group's brands.

Outback Steakhouse is offering a complimentary Bloomin' Onion and soft drink, along with a meal offer for a return visit, she said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Other deals listed in the guide include 10 free boneless wings and fries at Buffalo Wild Wings, a complimentary Red's Big Tavern Burger at Red Robin, free shrimp at Red Lobster and a free All-American Smash at Smashburger.

Dinova started the guide to share offers with veterans and, in some cases, active-duty military personnel, Quinn said. The company's business dining network includes about 25,000 restaurants and 600 corporate partners, she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Downloads of the guide have increased over the years, Quinn said, and the promotions may be useful for veterans or active-duty personnel who are struggling or "living under a tight budget."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Asked which deal she would choose, Quinn singled out Eddie Merlot's complimentary cheeseburger. Her father is an 85-year-old veteran, she said, and she plans to tell him about it.

Veterans and active-duty military members should bring identification and check with their local restaurant before visiting, Quinn said. Participation and ID requirements can vary by location and offer.

item.title: NYC man accused of 3 Central Park rapes arrested at Miami Burger King
item.description: A suspect was working at a Miami Beach Burger King when local police and U.S. Marshals arrested him over three alleged rapes reported in Central Park.
item.content:encoded:
A man suspected in three sexual assaults spanning five years in New York City's Central Park was arrested Tuesday at a Burger King in Miami Beach, Florida, authorities said.

Dereck Rivera-Deleon, 30, was taken into custody during an operation involving the NYPD, U.S. Marshals Service and Miami Beach police at a fast-food restaurant in the 1100 block of Washington Avenue.

"The NYPD will stop at nothing to get dangerous criminals off our streets," police said on X.

DEMS SILENT AFTER VIOLENT ATTACK IN WEALTHY AREA OF NEW YORK CITY AS SUSPECT REMAINS AT LARGE

Investigators located Rivera-Deleon in South Florida, where he had recently arrived and obtained employment at the restaurant, according to authorities.

The arrest followed an investigation into an Oct. 24 rape reported near Central Park's eastern edge in Manhattan.

An extraditable warrant was issued Monday in connection with the Oct. 24 assault.

Police said the attack happened at about 8:30 p.m. that night, when officers responded to a report of an assault near East 66th Street and Fifth Avenue.

The 39-year-old victim told investigators she was approached by a man who threatened her with a knife, forced her into a wooded section of the park and raped her before fleeing, according to police.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani previously described the attack as a "horrific" act.

Investigators also connected Rivera-Deleon to alleged sexual assaults in Central Park in 2021 and 2023 through DNA evidence and victim identifications, according to Miami Beach police. Authorities said he is expected to face charges in connection with both earlier incidents.

WOMAN FOUND DEAD WITH UNEXPLAINED TRAUMA IN CENTRAL PARK AS NYPD SEARCHES FOR ANSWERS

"When violent offenders flee to evade justice, we will ensure there is no corner of the country where they can hide," Ricky J. Patel, U.S. Marshal for the Southern District of New York, said in a statement.

Rivera-Deleon was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center in South Florida. He is being held without bond pending extradition proceedings to send him to New York to face sexual assault charges.

item.title: Multiple dead after vehicle crashes into food stand near North Hollywood Metro station
item.description: A car crashed into a food stand near a North Hollywood Metro bus stop on Tuesday, killing three and leaving multiple others critically injured.
item.content:encoded:
Three people were killed, and multiple others were injured after they were hit by a white SUV that crashed into a food stand near a North Hollywood Metro bus stop in Los Angeles on Tuesday night, according to authorities.

The collision was reported at around 5:55 p.m. near the Metro stop at the corner of Lankershim and Chandler boulevards, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.

"One vehicle reportedly involved with pedestrians," the fire department said in an alert.

SUSPECTED DRUNK DRIVER KILLS 2 PEDESTRIANS IN VIOLENT CHAIN-REACTION CRASH ON MANHATTAN'S UPPER WEST SIDE

The fire department said three people were pronounced dead at the scene.

Paramedics transported at least three others to a local hospital in critical condition, the department said.

"I'm heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted," Mayor Karen Bass said in a statement posted on X. "We will continue to provide updates as more information becomes available."

CALIFORNIA MOM HAS BOTH LEGS AMPUTATED AFTER SUSPECTED IMPAIRED DRIVER PLOWS INTO HER RESTAURANT LUNCH TABLE

The Los Angeles Police Department said the driver was hospitalized in critical condition after his white SUV struck at least five pedestrians, according to an LAPD statement posted on X. The man, who is in his 60s, is being evaluated by LAPD drug recognition experts to determine whether he was under the influence.

The circumstances surrounding the collision remain under investigation.

"It'll be a prolonged but a very deliberate investigation to determine what happened here," LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell told reporters. "Our hearts go out to the families of the victims that were struck here tonight."

item.title: Jaylen Brown repeatedly snubs ex-teammate Jayson Tatum as Celtics crush Sixers 'lambchops and some gravy'
item.description: Jaylen Brown gave Jayson Tatum the cold shoulder before tip-off in Philly, capping months of silence after a tense dinner confrontation in France.
item.content:encoded:
Former Celtics All-Star Jaylen Brown confronted ex-running mate Jayson Tatum at a dinner table in France last June over their future in Boston, and that bad blood finally resurfaced on the hardwood Tuesday night.

According to ESPN insider Shams Charania, that awkward European sit-down marked the last time the two stars spoke face-to-face.

GIANNIS ANTETOKOUNMPO ERA TO END IN MILWAUKEE AS BUCKS WILL SEND TWO-TIME MVP TO MIAMI HEAT FOR YOUNG CORE

Boston had just struck out on Giannis Antetokounmpo, who ended up in Miami instead. Celtics brass had put Brown on the table in those talks. Once Brown caught wind he was being shopped, he went straight to Tatum to find out where he stood and whether Tatum still wanted him in Boston.

Charania reported that Brown approached and confronted Tatum at the dinner table specifically to address their future as a tandem and gauge where Tatum stood on the entire situation.

Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia days later, effectively ending communication between the two. Tatum called and texted, but Brown never answered.

JAYLEN BROWN SOUNDS LIKE A 'SORE LOSER' AFTER BLAMING EMBIID FOR CELTICS' COLLAPSE

Seconds before tip-off Tuesday night in Philly, Tatum walked over and tapped Brown on the chest to say hello. Brown gave him absolute zero back. Eyes locked dead ahead, Brown didn't flinch, didn't dap him up, and blew right past him like Tatum wasn't there.

Asked before Tuesday's tip if he planned to clear the air, Brown said, "There's nothing to talk about." Brown then dropped the first on-court faceoff between the two, as Philadelphia fell 123-101 to Boston.

After the final buzzer, Brown hugged several of his former teammates before heading back to the locker room, leaving the floor without saying a word to Tatum.

Brown had 13 points against his former team. Tatum had 21 on 8-for-17 shooting.

When Tatum claimed on video last month that the trade caught him off guard, Brown hit back on Instagram with a blue cap emoji. Tatum tried shutting down the drama to reporters: "This ain't no f---ing Shaq and Kobe. There's no beef."

Brown countered on camera: "I saw that he said it's no beef and I think he's right. There's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family. We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He's got a great PR team. It's no beef. But it might be a little lambchops and some gravy."

Drafted third overall in back-to-back drafts (Brown in 2016, Tatum in 2017), the duo reached five conference finals, two NBA Finals and won the 2024 NBA title.

Debates over franchise ownership followed. Tatum earned First Team All-NBA nods, while Brown won the 2024 Eastern Conference Finals MVP and Finals MVP awards.

item.title: Former West Point cadet sued over alleged drugging, forced abortion of ex-girlfriend: 'Horrifying'
item.description: A former West Point cadet drugged his girlfriend and forced abortion pills into her mouth and vagina, according to a lawsuit filed by the victim.
item.content:encoded:
A former West Point cadet who pleaded guilty to drugging his then-girlfriend and administering abortion pills without her consent, causing a miscarriage, is facing a civil lawsuit that seeks unspecified damages.

Caleb Suh pleaded guilty in June to assault resulting in substantial bodily injury to a dating partner in connection with the March 2022 incident involving the woman, who was also a cadet at the U.S. Military Academy at the time.

Suh studied at two Ivy League universities since the incident, including one where he began attending classes after his guilty plea. He graduated from Cornell University this year and was enrolled as a graduate student at Columbia University when the woman filed a lawsuit Oct. 28.

The woman wanted to have the baby, but Suh did not want her to keep the child. Suh told the judge that he used the woman's identity to set up an online pharmacy account, ordered abortion drugs through the mail, obtained Xanax from a friend to use as a sedative and tricked his girlfriend into drinking what he claimed was a prenatal protein shake. When she fell asleep, Suh inserted the abortion pills into her mouth and vagina.

PRO-LIFE LEADER SOUNDS ALARM AFTER DOCTOR GETS 6 MONTHS FOR FORCING ABORTION PILLS ON GIRLFRIEND

Erin Hawley, a lawyer with the pro-life legal group Alliance Defending Freedom who played a key role in helping overturn Roe v. Wade, said the woman was put in an "absolutely horrific situation."

"She was expecting a child she very much wanted, was drugged and assaulted," Hawley, who is not representing the woman, told Fox News Digital. "The horrifying assault ended up causing the death of her very much wanted child — something no woman should ever have to endure. It has obviously caused a lot of harm and trauma, in addition to the loss of the baby she very much wanted."

"She was drugged and assaulted with abortion pills, even though Mr. Suh knew she very much wanted that child. I expect that he will be prosecuted to the full extent of the law," she added.

Suh is still awaiting sentencing.

Suh left the woman alone and incapacitated and ignored her attempts to reach him once she woke up and noticed that she was bleeding, according to the lawsuit. She was then hospitalized.

As the woman was receiving medical attention, Suh returned to the online pharmacy's website and posted questions about whether doctors could detect the medication he administered, according to the lawsuit.

"She’s suffered a life-changing event that she is still dealing with and will be dealing with for the rest of her life," her lawyer, Russell Kornblith, told The Associated Press last week.

"We hope that by our client coming forward with this lawsuit, it will, at least, ensure that this never happens to anyone else," Kornblith said.

INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM

Fox News Digital reached out to Suh's attorney for comment.

During a court hearing in June, Suh said that he was "deeply and immeasurably sorry for my actions and the pain that I have caused."

Suh's sentencing has been postponed until Jan. 21, 2027, at his attorney's request, allowing him to finish the semester at Columbia. Prosecutors did not oppose the delay for Suh's sentencing.

He has also been taking a three-month life skills course for people facing federal charges, his attorney said in a letter to the court.

Suh transferred to Cornell during the 2023-2024 school year. The university said in a statement last week that he answered "no" on an application when asked if he had been found responsible for a disciplinary violation at any previous institution.

The university said West Point noted that he was in good academic standing and was eligible to return. He had been involved in health and medicine at Cornell and wanted to become a physician, according to the university's website.

In September, Suh started a master's program at Columbia University's Mailman School of Public Health, his lawyer wrote to the judge in his federal case. A person familiar with the matter told The Associated Press that Mailman applicants are not asked about their criminal records but are questioned about whether they have ever been disciplined for student conduct violations or poor academic performance.

Suh’s application never made any mention of past disciplinary proceedings, the person told the outlet.

"Regardless of one’s position on abortion, it is not good medicine to allow an abortion drug to be shipped across the country to a dorm room or a home without a woman ever having talked to a doctor," Hawley said.

"The defendant in this case impersonated his girlfriend, had those drugs shipped and then assaulted her with them. That would never have happened if the FDA had done its job in 2023. Hopefully, when the courts do their job and reinstate that safeguard, it won’t continue to happen," she continued, referring to Alliance Defending Freedom's lawsuit challenging the Food and Drug Administration's 2023 decision to remove the in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone, after the agency had already stopped enforcing the requirement in 2021.

However, the assault occurred in March 2022, before the FDA's 2023 decision. The agency had already announced in April 2021 that it would temporarily stop enforcing the in-person dispensing requirement during the COVID-19 public health emergency. In December 2021, the FDA announced plans to permanently remove the requirement, a change formally implemented in January 2023.

The FDA has said its decision to remove the requirement followed a review of available evidence. Other restrictions, including prescriber certification requirements, remained in place.

Hawley added that the case at West Point would never have happened if that requirement had been in place.

"Horrific incidents like that throughout the country would never have happened if that basic safeguard had been in place," she said.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: College Football Playoff Rankings: Georgia rise to No. 1, Notre Dame cracks top 5 after big win over Miami
item.description: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish jumped six spots to No. 5 in the latest CFP rankings after their upset of No. 1 Miami, while Georgia takes the top spot now.
item.content:encoded:
The Notre Dame Fighting Irish, ranked No. 11 by the College Football Playoff committee in its initial rankings last week, took down the No. 1 team in the country, the Miami Hurricanes, in Week 10 to spoil their undefeated season.

As such, there’s a new top team in college football.

The Georgia Bulldogs, who blew out Ole Miss, 42-7, on the road, cemented themselves as the No. 1 team in the country. They were placed No. 2 behind Miami in the initial ranking given their blemish; A loss to Auburn back in October, had them at 7-1 entering Week 10.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Meanwhile, Miami plummeted down the rankings six spots after its one-touchdown loss to Notre Dame, moving to No. 7 overall. And the Fighting Irish jumped up six spots with that "signature" win under their belt at home against the top-ranked team, as they are now at No. 5.

But these rankings will surely stir some debate, as Alabama, picking up a commanding 31-13 win over LSU, moved up two spots to No. 3 with a 7-2 record. Utah is above them at No. 2 overall, yet UCLA, who shares the same 9-0 record as the Utes, is No. 4 underneath a two-loss team.

While that will surely stir up the SEC bias argument on social media and beyond, Tennessee came in at No. 8 after a big win over Kentucky, which the committee has at No. 11 in their latest rankings. Both the Vols and Crimson Tide own a 7-2 record, and the head-to-head question that arose in last week’s rankings is even stronger now since Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 earlier this season.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF COMMITTEE EXECUTIVE ADMITS THEY DON'T CARE FANS ARE AGAINST 24-TEAM PLAYOFF

CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek, who serves as athletic director for Arkansas, explained Alabama’s placement.

"They’re number one in record strength. Number one in their schedule strength," he said. "They have four, what we call, quality wins, because we continue to call that the win against Mississippi State earlier in the year when they had Kamario Taylor on their team. They were 4-0. Alabama went there and won that game. So, Alabama, we believe, deserves to be the No. 3 team in the country."

And why wasn’t Tennessee ranked higher?

"Well, we’ll go back to what you just said about Miami and Notre Dame. Alabama was in that first pool – Tennessee was not in that first pool," Yurachek said, referring to the subgroups teams are placed in based on metrics, with the first pool being the top teams in the country in the committee’s eyes. "Tennessee’s got a couple of quality wins – their win they just had against Kentucky and the win they had against Alabama."

Texas came in at No. 6, and after No. 7 Miami and No. 8 Tennessee, we find Indiana, coming off a bye week, sitting at No. 9. They dropped five spots as their key wins earlier this season didn’t look as strong, though the reigning champs remain 8-1.

At No. 10, BYU comes off a wild one against Utah, where they came back in the game on the road only to lose to the No. 2 team in the country. Kentucky is No. 11, Texas Tech is No. 12, and Wake Forest, Houston and Iowa round out the top 15, respectively.

At No. 16, Oregon has leaped seven spots following its 41-28 win over Ohio State, which plummeted eight spots to No. 20 after back-to-back losses that pushed them to 6-3 on the season.

Ole Miss, coming in at No. 19, also fell hard (nine spots) following the blowout home loss to Georgia.

item.title: Stacy Keach dead at 85 as ‘Mike Hammer’ star’s wife shares emotional tribute
item.description: Stacy Keach's wife reveals the lengthy heart failure battle behind the iconic Mike Hammer actor's final days and his extraordinary courage.
item.content:encoded:
Stacy Keach, the legendary actor whose unmistakable voice and powerful performances captivated generations of Americans, is being remembered by his beloved wife as a devoted husband, loving father and courageous fighter after his death at 85.

Keach, best known for portraying the hard-boiled private detective Mike Hammer and for his celebrated work on stage and screen, died Tuesday, Nov. 10, at his family home in Magdalenka, Poland.

His wife, Małgosia Tomassi Keach, shared an emotional statement announcing his passing following a lengthy battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure.

PATRICK STEWART, LEGENDARY 'STAR TREK' AND 'X-MEN' ACTOR, DIES AT 86

"It is with profound sadness and a broken heart that I announce the passing of my darling husband, Stacy Keach," she said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

"After a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, Stacy peacefully departed this world. He fought for so long, with extraordinary courage, determination and strength."

She remembered her husband as a man whose remarkable resilience extended far beyond the characters he brought to life on-screen.

"He was a true warrior, facing his illness with the same remarkable spirit and resilience that defined his life," she continued.

'TOP GUN' STAR TOM SKERRITT DEAD AT 93

"Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family."

For millions of television viewers, Keach will forever be remembered as Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer, the tough-talking private investigator he portrayed with grit, charisma and an unmistakable screen presence.

EVA MARIE SAINT, OSCAR-WINNING ‘ON THE WATERFRONT’ AND ‘NORTH BY NORTHWEST’ STAR, DEAD AT 102

But his extraordinary career stretched far beyond the detective series. A gifted Shakespearean actor, Keach tackled some of theater's most demanding roles, including Hamlet, Richard III and King Lear. He also earned a Golden Globe for his portrayal of Ernest Hemingway.

His television appearances included "Blue Bloods," "Titus" and "Prison Break," while his film credits ranged from "The Long Riders" to "Nebraska" and "The Bourne Legacy."

Keach also appeared in the Biblical miniseries "Jesus of Nazareth," portraying the criminal Barabbas.

In 2017, Keach suffered a heart attack while performing in a one-man production about Ernest Hemingway at Chicago's Goodman Theatre, an ordeal that forced the cancellation of the show's run.

Throughout a career spanning more than six decades, Keach earned admiration not only for his versatility but also for the unmistakable voice and commanding presence that made him one of Hollywood's most recognizable performers.

Yet for those closest to him, his greatest legacy was the love he shared with his family.

"His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives," his wife said. "But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever."

Keach is survived by his wife, their children, Karolina and Shannon, and their extended family. His family's farewell was signed with profound love and sorrow by Małgosia, Karolina, Shannon, their grandchildren and spouses.

The Associated Press contributed to this reporting.

item.title: ESPN dismisses Utah Utes as National Championship contenders despite big win over BYU: 'They won't win'
item.description: Utah football climbed to No. 2 in the AP Poll after beating BYU Cougars in the Holy War, but ESPN analysts question their national championship hopes.
item.content:encoded:
One of the signature wins of the 2026 college football season was the BYU Cougars taking down the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in Provo. For BYU, it gave them a massive resume boost, while making it clear that the Big 12 Conference was relevant at a national level.

BYU immediately became a clear College Football Playoff contender, and staked their claim as a top-5 or top-10 team. The Cougars though, suffered a letdown against a very mediocre UCF team in Florida, taking a bit of the shine off their matchup against the Utah Utes on November 7.

The quality of the "Holy War" though? Anyone watching saw that those were clearly two of the best teams in the country. Yes, Utah won 28-20, but it was a back-and-forth battle in an intense rivalry game. And again, handed a big win to a Big 12 Conference team.

NO 3 UTAH REMAINS UNDEFEATED WITH THRILLING WIN OVER NO 9 BYU BEHIND HEISMAN FINALIST DEVON DAMPIER'S EPIC DAY

Utah's comeback catapulted them to No. 2 in the latest AP Top 25 Poll, behind only the Georgia Bulldogs. They're 9-0 in a Power 4 conference, with wins over a quality top-15 Houston Cougars team and the BYU win. They're odds-on favorites to reach the playoff, and now favorites to win the Big 12 Conference and likely secure a first-round bye. By any objective measure, they're legitimate contenders to win a National Championship.

But ESPN is not objective.

Senior analyst Heather Didich, one of the more prominent SEC boosters on a network known for them, threw cold water on Utah's hopes in a recent episode of ESPN's "Get Up" show.

"They are there by default because some other teams above them lost. They have a great quarterback in Devon Dampier. This selection committee has a lot of respect for Utah. They're a good football team. Are they a great football team? I don't think we know the answer to that. I hesitate to say yes because they struggled to beat Colorado," she said.

BYU HAS THRIVED IN AN NIL ERA THAT MANY EXPECTED THEM TO FALTER IN, NFL LEGEND STEVE YOUNG SAYS

Didich continued, saying that the win over BYU was aided by Bear Bachmeier's mistake-filled game and that she doubts whether they can win a title.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"This was the first real big win for them, in my mind, and, by the way, BYU and Bear Bachmeier helped them out with four interceptions and a boatload of penalties. So, I still have some questions about Utah in terms of how they stack up against a team like Georgia. But, sitting there at number two, that's where I expect them to be. They can compete for the national title. I don't know if they're good enough to win it," she added.

Paul Finebaum was even more definitive.

"They are not good enough to win it, Greeny," he said. "Let me just get that out of the way. I didn't mean to jump in, but I'll clear that up for America. They will not win the national championship."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The comparisons to Georgia are interesting, because, as fans will remember, the Bulldogs lost, at home, to Auburn. Auburn is now 5-4, with a home loss to Florida, at Tennessee, a 38-17 blowout loss to LSU at home, a 30-point loss to Ole Miss, and a close home win over a bad Arkansas team.

Yes, UGA has played a tougher schedule, but Utah's played their schedule without losing. And dismissing their season because of a close game against Colorado while dismissing Georgia's, or any number of other team's slip-ups, is only done because of obvious bias.

We can also look at ESPN's SP+ to see why. An objective, efficiency-driven and opponent-adjusted ranking system based on success rate on offense, defense, and special teams, it's a better measurement of which teams are legitimate contenders and which aren't.

While Utah is No. 9 in this week's update, SEC darling Alabama is ... No. 8. If Alabama is a championship contender, so's Utah. In fact, while Texas is No. 6, their "rating" at 23.5 implies they'd be just two-point favorites on a neutral field over Utah, with their 21.5 rating. Two points is marginally different from a toss-up. And toss-up games can, obviously, go either way.

Will the Utes win a title? Who knows! It's a long road through the playoff, and injuries or a bounce here or there can change a game and a season. But one thing is beyond question; that ESPN would not be dismissing their chances if they wore a different patch. They'd be knocking down doors to get them to No. 1.

item.title: Mullin vows ‘zero change’ on immigration after Republicans suffer crushing midterm losses
item.description: Markwayne Mullin says the Department of Homeland Security is deporting roughly 3,600 people a day and promises "zero change" after midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin delivered a blunt message on immigration policy Tuesday, promising "zero change" following midterm elections that dealt a crushing blow to the Republican Party.

Mullin made the remarks during an appearance on Fox News' "The Ingraham Angle," where host Laura Ingraham brought up President Donald Trump suggesting Republicans work with Democrats.

"Amnesty will never be on the table," Mullin said.

WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS

He noted that the agency has been deporting roughly 3,600 individuals a day and has no plans to slow down.

"We haven't slowed down at all. We've re-prioritize what we're doing by going after the worst of the worst, by getting the murderers and the rapists and child predators and drug bankers and cartel members," he added.

While Democrats secured majorities in both the House and Senate during the midterm elections, Mullin said Republicans cannot trust the opposing party to work with them.

"You can't trust the Democrat Party we've been working with at all. You can't, because nothing's enough for them," he said.

He also criticized the Democratic Party's leadership, pointing to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and accusing the group of wanting to "defund the country."

"You got DSA that's running the Democrat Party right now. They want to defund my agency, the Department of Homeland Security," he said.

BORDER DEM POISED TO WIELD ICE PURSE STRINGS REJECTS SOCIALIST ‘DEFUND’ PUSH

"You want to defund the country that is the agency that's tasked with keeping our homeland safe? Doesn’t make any sense," he added.

Mullin also recalled Trump's comments about using his veto power if Democrats pass measures he opposes.

"The president has made it very clear he controls the veto. So if they were to send something over that the president and the Republicans don't agree with, he can veto it, and he will veto it," he said.

"The president will not sign anything that isn't in the right movement for this country and the Republican Party."

Mullin also argued that maintaining a strong immigration policy is imperative to national security.

"You can't have a secured nation and you can't have a secured city if you don't know who's in your country," he said.

item.title: Brittany Mahomes announces baby No. 4 as Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs gear up for AFC push
item.description: Chiefs Kingdom is on baby watch after Brittany Mahomes announced baby No. 4 with beachside photos, fueling speculation over another metals name.
item.content:encoded:
The Mahomes household is growing again, and Chiefs Kingdom is officially back on baby watch.

item.title: Maddow fears Trump migrant detention centers may be used to imprison ‘the rest of us’

item.content:encoded:

Host Jon Stewart and Maddow discussed the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) decision to cancel plans to build a 10,000-detainee immigration center in a commercial warehouse in Social Circle, Georgia, after the proposal faced local opposition.

"Social circle stood up for itself," Maddow said. "You know, people all over the country where Trump wanted to put these mega prisons, these were huge warehouses to hold people by the thousands. Places that would hold five, six, seven, ten, 14,000 people, all without trial, held indefinitely."

TRUMP ADMIN CANNOT REFUSE DETAINED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS A CHANCE FOR RELEASE ON BOND, APPEALS COURT RULES

"These are people who overstayed a student visa or are here on a green card but got a parking ticket, like ticky-tack s--- that normally would be treated civilly," he said.

Maddow acknowledged that other scenarios were possible but suggested that concerns about Trump’s new detention centers should extend beyond immigrant advocates.

"No, I'm sorry, with a president like this, if you give him seven to ten prisons around the country that hold 10,000 people each, where he can hold people without trial, without access to lawyers, indefinitely, you think he's only going to leave immigrants in there?" she asked.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT COMPARES TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION POLICY TO JAPANESE AMERICAN INTERNMENT

EXCLUSIVE: ICE CAPTURES ILLEGAL ALIEN AT CENTER OF NYC MANHUNT AFTER SANCTUARY CITY RELEASE

item.title: Turning Point USA Spox Andrew Kolvet speaks out as Jennifer Welch, Dave Chappelle mock Charlie Kirk's murder
item.description: Andrew Kolvet slams Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan's apology as narcissistic and calls Dave Chappelle's remarks about Charlie Kirk deeply disappointing.
item.content:encoded:
Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet is firing back at "I've Had It" podcast hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan and comedian Dave Chappelle for making light of Charlie Kirk's murder in recent days.

"We're not asking people to, you know, be evangelical Christians here. We're asking don't celebrate, condone or glorify political violence. Don't be happy when someone's assassinated. It's a very, very low bar," Kolvet told Fox News Digital in an interview.

Last week, Welch and Sullivan sparked backlash for laughing uncontrollably while reading an online post that read, "We're digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again" as they celebrated Democratic victories in the 2026 midterms. 

After several sponsors pulled their ads, Welch and Sullivan issued an apology, though Welch later insisted it wasn't meant for Kolvet or others offended by the mockery, saying the apology "was for us."

WELCH DOUBLES DOWN ON TPUSA FEUD, CALLS GROUP 'LOSERS' AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT KILLING CHARLIE KIRK AGAIN

"Pro tip, an apology is for the other person," Kolvet reacted to Welch. "It is for people that you've aggrieved and hurt. It's not for you, unless you're a narcissist. And then I guess it is about you. So, that was pretty shocking."

Several sponsors have dropped the podcast since Welch and Sullivan's laughing fit went viral over the past several days. Though he said neither he nor TPUSA were behind what he calls the "grassroots" boycott movement against the podcast, he celebrated the decision reached by various companies once associated with the show.

"I'm generally not pro-cancel culture, but I also believe that these brands get their own free speech," Kolvet said. "These brands get to have the speech to say, 'I don't want to be associated with somebody that celebrates the murder of an innocent man because of his politics.'

CHAPPELLE, JENNIFER WELCH JOKES ABOUT KIRK'S MURDER PART OF PATTERN OF LEFTISTS FINDING HUMOR IN VIOLENCE

"I'm not asking for Jennifer Welch to be imprisoned. I'm not asking for her to not have a show or to be able to express her opinions. ... All I'm saying is it's not that hard. Don't celebrate political violence," he continued. 

"Don't laugh at it. Don't rub it in our faces that one of the most important people in the conservative movement in the country for Gen Z was murdered in cold blood. Don't do it. Don't be a ghoul, don't be vile, don't spew that venom and don't perpetuate that culture.

"Cause when you do, you're participating in something very dark and brands, consumers, Americans all have a right to say what they feel about your antics and your behavior," Kolvet added.

He said Welch's "apology" ended up doing more harm to her and her podcast than good and rejected her assertion that the boycott movement was TPUSA attempting to wage war on her podcast.

"Nobody's done this to you, Jennifer. You've done this to yourself," he told Welch. "I don't expect you to listen to me but maybe, just maybe you will listen to all those brands who no longer want to be associated with you."

HOW CHARLIE KIRK’S ASSASSINATION CHANGED THE WAY CONSERVATIVES APPROACH HOSTILE OPPONENTS

Despite Welch's "petty" insistence that she would never sit down with him, Kolvet said he would "totally sit down with her."

"I wouldn't do it for content. I would sit down in a closed-door space, and my heart would be open, and I would be generous and gracious to her and hope that it would be a fruitful conversation," he said. "My expectation for that is infinitesimally low, but certainly I would be open to that.

"You know, Charlie modeled that," Kolvet continued. "He was willing to talk to anybody. He was willing to talk to people that hated his guts. ... But Charlie wanted to have those conversations because he knew that once conversations stopped happening, that's when violence happens.

"And, so, our conversation, our debate is an escape hatch," he added. "It's a release valve for the tensions in our culture. And, you know, hopefully she changes her mind and her posture about having conversations with people that don't agree with her completely."

Regarding Chappelle, Kolvet said he has no intention to "speech police him" but that what he told a crowd at Madison Square Garden that he "feel[s] better" after Kirk's assassination was "a really crazy thing to say."

Kolvet hearkened back to the nation's response to the 1981 assassination attempt on President Ronald Reagan, saying he learned from reports at the time that only one obscure comedian cracked a joke about it at a Los Angeles comedy club. He noted that the joke "bombed" and pointed out that the Academy Awards ceremony was delayed by a day out of respect for the recovering president.

"Ronald Reagan was not a popular president in the media in 1981. He was much maligned, as a matter of fact, but the country as a whole understood that political assassination is an evil, evil thing," Kolvet said.

Kirk defended Chappelle in 2022 after a man attacked the comedian while he was performing at the Hollywood Bowl after controversy over his jokes about transgender people.

SOCIAL MEDIA HORRIFIED BY DAVE CHAPPELLE’S SICK ‘JOKE’ ABOUT CHARLIE KIRK’S MURDER

"Charlie saw the writing on the wall," Kolvet told Fox News Digital. "Charlie was always warning against the rise of political violence, warning against the rise of assassination culture. And, obviously, it's deeply disappointing that Dave Chappelle couldn't return those sympathies to Charlie when Charlie lost his life.

"We need to be kind to our fellow Americans," he continued. "We need to wish the best for them. We need to hope for their safety and that just because I disagree with you politically doesn't mean that I wish ill upon you or physical harm. As a matter of fact, I hope you're safe, and I hope that you live a long life and I hope I can convince you on the merits of my arguments, or you can convince me of yours.

"But political violence is not something to be toyed around with, and our culture literally depends on us having a bright line right there," Kolvet said. 

"I want to live in a culture where comedians don't even tell those jokes because they know nobody's going to laugh," he added. "And that's the best way to make sure that we're not replaying the same scene a hundred times more in the future."

item.title: Biden reveals letter Trump left him at White House that made it seem 'as if there were two Donald Trumps'
item.description: President Donald Trump's letter to former President Joe Biden, sent weeks after the January 6 Capitol riots in 2021, offered warm wishes, Biden's new memoir revealed.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden revealed in his upcoming memoir, "Promise Me, America," that President Donald Trump left him an unexpectedly friendly letter in January 2021 before Biden entered office after defeating Trump in the 2020 election, according to a report published Tuesday.

According to an excerpt obtained by The New York Times, Biden reprinted the letter in full in his upcoming book, which is scheduled for release next week. In it, Biden wrote that it seemed "as if there were two Donald Trumps."

He contrasted the public-facing Trump who "deeply destabilized our democracy" and had "not offered the traditional meeting between presidents" with the one who in the letter was "offering his best wishes in warm language that sounded like it was coming from an old friend."

JOE BIDEN ADDRESSES CRITICS WHO SAID HE HID HIS STAGE 4 CANCER DIAGNOSIS IN UPCOMING MEMOIR

"You now have the opportunity to choose your place in history, and I know you will be true to yourself and the American people," Trump wrote in the letter, according to Biden. 

"Many presidents have come and gone who simply governed as Republicans or Democrats. Largely, they did not change history, they were just swept along in its relentless tide. This will not happen to you because I know how much you love the American people.

"Your strength, your deepest reservoir of energy, comes from the knowledge that millions upon millions of people are depending on you. Their ambitions and aspirations are the reason you are here, with so many counting on your success," he added. "May God bless you and Jill, and may God bless America!"

The Atlantic also highlighted a passage from the book recounting Biden’s customary 2024 White House meeting with Trump. Biden noted that the incoming president once again displayed a warm side, writing, "Trump was immediately chatty and surprised me by adopting a tone so friendly that I thought he might be putting me on. It bordered on fawning."

BILL MAHER CLAIMS DONALD TRUMP FELT 'BETRAYED' BY HIM WITH 'SILLY' FEUD AFTER CORDIAL 2025 DINNER

"You know, Joe, if it weren’t for politics, I believe we’d be good friends," Trump told him, according to The Atlantic report. "Yes, if it weren’t for politics, we’d spend all our time golfing together."

Biden's friendly reception of Trump during the meeting also drew attention. Biden repeatedly argued while he was still running that Trump was "a threat to democracy."

Radio host Charlamagne Tha God questioned Biden's reception of Trump on his radio show at the time.

"I just don't understand the White House visit. Now granted, you know, I'm glad it's a peaceful transition of power, but what happened to the ‘threat of democracy’ talk? What happened to the ‘fascist’ talk?" Charlamagne asked. 

"By the way, I know I've said those things about Trump as well, but I'm not talking about me, I'm talking about his political opponents, like President Biden. When they say it, it holds way more weight than me.

"I'm just trying to figure out, how do you go from ‘He's an existential threat to democracy’ to ‘Welcome back?’"

CHARLAMAGNE RIPS JILL BIDEN’S CONFESSIONS ABOUT HER HUSBAND AS TOO LITTLE, TOO LATE

White House communications director Steven Cheung responded to Biden's comments in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Joe Biden should have heeded the President’s wise words, but instead he tried to destroy this country and weaponize the justice system against his political enemies. Biden is a disgrace, and America is better off with him no longer as president," Cheung said.

Theo Wold, a former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy during Trump's first term, also spoke to Fox News Digital about the report.

"This is another example of the 'when-they-go-low-we-go-high' people doing exactly the opposite. President Trump left a magnanimous letter to Biden, impressing upon him the weight of the job and the responsibility every president bears to the American people. And Biden uses it only to tear down Trump, suggesting insincerity," Wold said. 

"No. Democrats — including the team of leftist ghostwriters that penned this book for Biden — want to hate Trump, and so they will, regardless of any evidence showing their hatred is unfounded."

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden's office for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: IRGC operative lands on FBI’s Most Wanted Terrorists list over alleged plot to kill former Trump advisor
item.description: Shahram Poursafi allegedly sought to pay $300,000 to have John Bolton killed in a plot authorities linked to retaliation for Qasem Soleimani’s death.
item.content:encoded:
The FBI on Tuesday placed a member of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on its Most Wanted Terrorists list for allegedly soliciting the murders of two former U.S. government officials.

Shahram Poursafi is accused of hiring individuals to kill the officials between October 2021 and April 2022, according to the FBI’s Washington Field Office. Court documents detail an alleged plot targeting former National Security Advisor John Bolton.

The assassination plot was believed to have been initiated in retaliation for the January 2020 killing of IRGC commander Qasem Soleimani, who led a unit of the Qods Force, one of the IRGC's five divisions responsible for developing and carrying out lethal plotting operations.

Poursafi allegedly worked on behalf of the division and sought to pay individuals in the U.S. $300,000 to carry out the assassination.

US OFFERS $20M FOR IRANIAN IN PLOT TARGETING TRUMP’S EX-NATIONAL SECURITY ADVISER JOHN BOLTON

Separately, the FBI released wanted posters seeking information on three alleged IRGC officials from the same Qods Force unit. The individuals were identified as Mohammad Reza Ansari, Abolfazl Alizadeh and Mohammad Hossein Shamoradizadeh.

Ansari is an alleged deputy who has supported IRGC operations in Syria. He also allegedly planned and attempted to assassinate two former U.S. government officials with the Poursafi’s support.

Alizadeh and Shamoradizadeh are both alleged battalion commanders who have participated in lethal plotting operations.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

According to a 2022 Justice Department complaint announcing the charges against Poursafi, Poursafi initially plotted the assassination by asking a U.S. resident he had previously met online to take photographs of Bolton, claiming the images were for a book he was writing.

Poursafi later offered another U.S. contact up to $300,000 to "eliminate" the former national security advisor. Poursafi also told the contact he had an additional "job" for which he would pay $1 million.

BOLTON CALLS IRAN ASSASSINATION PLOT AN 'ACT OF WAR,' CALLS ON BIDEN ADMIN TO 'TERMINATE' NUCLEAR TALKS

The plot ultimately fell through as the contact was a confidential human source working with the FBI, often considered civilian informants.

Poursafi was charged with using communication or travel networks across state lines to carry out a paid assassination. He was also accused of supplying resources or assistance for an international murder plot, according to a Justice Department complaint.

A special agent in charge of the FBI's Washington Field Office said the agency will continue to disrupt lethal plots and bring IRGC members to justice for threatening U.S. individuals.

"The FBI will not stand for the IRGC’s brazen attempts to silence, harm or murder activists, dissidents, journalists, public officials or anyone else it deems a threat," Gregory Heeb of the FBI Washington Field Office’s Counterterrorism Division said.

item.title: US evacuates 13 military aircraft from second UK base as new Iran threat raises alarm
item.description: More than a dozen U.S. Air Force aircraft left RAF Mildenhall after a reported Iran-linked threat triggered the second-highest military alert level.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Air Force abruptly relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England amid an emerging security threat, U.S. officials confirmed Tuesday.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the move, citing sources who said the threat originated in Iran.

As U.S. officials assessed the threat's nature and urgency, commanders raised the base's security level to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the military's second-highest alert level, indicating a likely terrorist threat against personnel or facilities.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

Flight-tracking data and open-source analysts with the Military Air Tracking Alliance identified 13 U.S. aircraft leaving the base late Monday, the Associated Press said.

Nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers were moved to airfields in Scotland, Germany and Spain.

Three CV-22B Ospreys were relocated to nearby RAF Lakenheath, which has hardened aircraft shelters.

A U.S. official told The Associated Press the moves were precautionary, noting that some aircraft were on rotational deployments while others were permanently stationed in the United Kingdom.

IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY

The move marks the second major relocation of U.S. military aircraft from Britain in less than two months.

In early October, the Air Force pulled heavy bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire after British counterterrorism police stopped three suspicious vans headed toward the base Sept. 27.

Two men have since been charged under the United Kingdom's National Security Act.

Separately, the Justice Department unsealed indictments against three Iranian-backed operatives on Tuesday accused of involvement in coordinated terrorist plots across Europe, including RAF Fairford.

UK POLICE ARREST 'EXPLOSIVE' SUSPECTS NEAR US AIRBASE, KEY TO IRAN WAR

RAF Mildenhall is home to the 100th Air Refueling Wing, the only permanently based U.S. tanker wing in Europe.

Its KC-135 Stratotankers support allied aerial refueling and long-range strike missions across the region.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that Washington routinely repositions military forces.

"We are constantly repositioning forces around the world for a variety of reasons," Rubio told reporters when asked about the evacuation.

A 10 Downing Street spokesperson said British air bases remain secure and that London and Washington continuously share intelligence on potential threats.

In the film, Curry’s character believes the odds are stacked against her after a string of relationships she considers unsuccessful. Her outlook changes when she reconnects with her former high school sweetheart, played by Daddario.

Curry said she was drawn to the film’s holiday backdrop and the opportunity to bring her character, Chelsey, to life.

"It’s an honor to be part of Second Chance Holiday alongside such a talented cast and crew," Curry said in a statement released in July. "There’s something truly magical about holiday rom-coms. They invite you into these charming, cozy worlds where anything feels possible. Chelsey is such a fun, heartfelt character that I fell in love with while bringing her to life. I hope audiences fall in love with her too and enjoy Second Chance Holiday this holiday season."

item.title: Cardinals star Michael Wilson out for remainder of the season with neck fracture in crushing blow, coach says
item.description: Michael Wilson played through a neck fracture against the Seattle Seahawks before the Arizona Cardinals learned their No. 1 wide receiver is done for the year.
item.content:encoded:
Arizona Cardinals star wide receiver Michael Wilson is out for the season after suffering a fracture in his neck.

Wilson, 26, suffered the injury on the fourth play of the Cardinals’ 17-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, but continued to play. He caught a 17-yard pass and landed on his head after being tackled by cornerback Devon Witherspoon.

"He said (during the game) he kind of had a kink in his neck, but he's such a warrior you didn't think much of it," head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Monday. "Then obviously when the adrenaline wore down and he got his test today, that's when we knew."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Cardinals officially placed Wilson on IR on Tuesday.

Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million extension before Week 1 after emerging as Cardinals' No. 1 wide receiver. In nine games this season, Wilson had 51 catches for 546 yards and two touchdowns.

Last season, Wilson had 78 catches for 1,006 yards with seven touchdowns. With Wilson injured and Marvin Harrison Jr. traded in October, the Cardinals are dangerously thin at wide receiver.

Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay, Reggie Virgil and Harrison Wallace are the four remaining wide receivers on the active roster. LaFleur said Wilson’s injury creates opportunities for other players to step up and show what they can do.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The lack of wide receiver options will likely mean even more targets for superstar tight end Trey McBride.

McBride has 73 receptions, the most in the NFL, along with 598 yards and five touchdowns.

Unfortunately for the Cardinals, the injury news didn’t stop with Wilson.

Starting quarterback Gardner Minshew may need season-ending surgery to repair the ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow, according to ESPN. The Cardinals recently traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, so rookie quarterback Carson Beck would start if Minshew is unable to play.

Beck would face difficult circumstances, as star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is on injured reserve , and the team's wide receiver group consists largely of unproven players.

The Cardinals' (3-6) next game is against the Los Angeles Rams (5-4) at home on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET.

item.title: 'I've Had It' host Jennifer Welch cheers Wisconsin brewing company that called Kirk an 'awful human being'
item.description: Jennifer Welch promoted the Minocqua Brewing Company on her "I've Had It" podcast after the Wisconsin anti-Trump brewery attacked Charlie Kirk and offered sponsorship.
item.content:encoded:
"I've Had It" podcast host Jennifer Welch endorsed the anti-Trump Wisconsin brewery Minocqua Brewing Company on her podcast Tuesday after it referred to Turning Point USA (TPUSA) founder Charlie Kirk as a "racist jerk" and "awful human being."

The show's producer, Kiley Josey, read a Facebook post from Sunday from the business attacking sponsors for pulling their support of Welch after she and co-host Angie Sullivan laughed at a joke about digging up Kirk's body after his assassination last year.

In the post, Minocqua Brewing Company offered to support the podcast with a sponsorship, attacking Kirk in the process.

LIBERAL PODCASTERS TELL TPUSA TO ‘F--- OFF’ AS CHARLIE KIRK BACKLASH COSTS THEM ADVERTISERS

"Charlie Kirk was an awful human being, and everybody who’s not in a cult or a paid influencer on the right realizes that," the post read. 

"We’re sorry you’ve lost a few sponsors because you laughed at a joke about this racist jerk. We probably don’t have as much money as the sponsors you lost, but we’d love to step in and partner with you if you'll have us."

"That is so sweet," Welch said. "Well, Minocqua Brewing Company, shout out to you and no money necessary. We are happy to promote your products and everybody in Wisconsin if you're … I don't know if their products are online, but hit up the Minocqua Brewing Company."

Josey also described how the brewery has sold merchandise attacking President Donald Trump and the Republican Party, earning more praise from Welch.

WELCH DOUBLES DOWN ON TPUSA FEUD, CALLS GROUP 'LOSERS' AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT KILLING CHARLIE KIRK AGAIN

"Anti-Trump merch. You know what? I mean free ads for them forever. Forever. They're doing the good work. And I love a business that says we stand on business, and we're not going to tolerate our customer base being treated like s---. If other businesses could only say the same," Welch said.

Minocqua Brewing Company previously gained nationwide attention after promoting a deal for "free beer, all day long" on the day Trump dies. The company doubled down on the deal after a foiled attack at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in April.

"Well, we almost got #freebeerday," the company's post at the time said. "Either a brother or sister in the Resistance needs to work on their marksmanship or he faked another assassination to get a positive news cycle. We’ll never know."

FBI, SECRET SERVICE PROBE WISCONSIN BREWERY OWNER OVER FREE BEER OFFER AFTER ALLEGED TRUMP KILLING ATTEMPT

In a comment to Fox News Digital, Welch clarified, "We have never heard of Minocqua Brewing Company before today. Neither of us drink. Several listeners tagged us in a post from this company, and we read the post on the show without knowing of their previous comments. We have no relationship with this company and don’t intend to have one."

TPUSA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet told Fox News Digital, "Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan have nobody to blame but themselves for the fact that their sponsors are cutting ties. Rather than accept responsibility for their own behavior, they want to blame Turning Point for noticing.

"The organization didn’t coordinate this boycott; it happened organically. Everyday Americans were fed up with the fact they consistently laugh at, snicker, sneer and generally glorify assassination culture on their podcast. The audience — and their sponsors — are shouting at them that there is a line and they crossed it. They just refuse to listen."

Fox News Digital also reached out to Minocqua Brewing Company, but it declined to comment on the matter.

item.title: SEC head Greg Sankey blasts announcers for criticizing poor officiating in Texas-Missouri: 'Unacceptable'
item.description: Greg Sankey attacked announcers for criticizing SEC officiating after the Texas Longhorns-Missouri Tigers game, drawing a rebuke from Terry McAuley.
item.content:encoded:
For most neutral fans and viewers watching Saturday's game between the Texas Longhorns and Missouri Tigers, there was a clear and obvious issue with the officiating.

A number of calls were either seemingly mishandled, called incorrectly or slanted in favor of one side or the other. More often than not, in the Longhorns' direction. To the point where the announcers covering the game, Joe Tessitore and Jesse Palmer, commented on it.

Palmer at one point during the game was very forthcoming, saying he'd be furious if he were a Missouri fan.

MIAMI COACH FURIOUS WITH OFFICIALS AFTER POSSIBLE TD CATCH RULED INCOMPLETE IN CRUCIAL LOSS TO NOTRE DAME

"I’m just going to say this. No skin in the game, [but] if you’re a Missouri fan, if you’re Eli Drinkwitz, you are livid," he said. "Because it does feel like a lot of these calls are going against Missouri today."

He said it again later, in the fourth quarter. The refs missed a key penalty when a Texas defender forcibly knocked over a Missouri wide receiver away from the play, which should have resulted in an unnecessary roughness penalty and a free first down and 15-yards. Instead, no call, and Palmer was once again flabbergasted.

REFS' CRUCIAL NO CALL LOOMS LARGE OVER GEORGIA'S VICTORY OVER ALABAMA

"I can’t believe I’m saying this ... but I think on that last play, this reffing crew missed another call that negatively impacts Missouri," he said.

One of the most obvious and controversial calls was the "fumble" from Texas QB Arch Manning on a third down play in the third quarter. Manning's arm appeared to be coming forward as the ball left his hand, which would have made the play an incomplete pass and forced a tough decision from Texas coach Steve Sarkisian. Instead, it was ruled a fumble, with a clear recovery from the Longhorns, resulting in a pick-up of 14-yards and a first down. They went down and scored immediately afterward, helping jumpstart the win.

That call drew immense criticism from all corners of the college football world, especially for how it impacted the outcome of the game. Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz was, as Palmer suggested, livid: "If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not going to do that. I'm not going to blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach Sarkisian and his team," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Well, SEC commissioner Greg Sankey clearly heard those complaints and instead of addressing the referees and their calls, he chose to ... attack the announcers.

BIG 12 CONFERENCE ADMITS OFFICIALS GOT CALL WRONG THAT BENEFITED BYU COUGARS IN WIN OVER ARIZONA STATE

"I am highly disappointed in announcers and their criticism, and they're wrong," he said on "The Paul Finebaum Show." "Some of the worst officials in America are those in the announcers booth.

"We have officiating experts, who I turned on a game on Saturday, who was just flat wrong," he continued. "And what that creates is this narrative that we've done something wrong and that is unacceptable to me, and we have to address that."

Remember, the officiating in that game was so controversial that the Missouri athletic director, Laird Veatch, published an open letter asking for more transparency from the SEC. Sankey choosing to go after the announcers instead though, is par for the course.

Officiating expert and NBC rules analyst Terry McAuley saw Sankey's interview, and took the time to respond to it in a post on X.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

"Football announcers in both college and the NFL in today's world are far more knowledgeable about rules than they have ever been in my lifetime. They are also more supportive of officiating than they have ever been. The three announcing crews I regularly work with are incredibly strong on their knowledge of the rules, which (fortunately?) minimizes the times I need to speak.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Sometimes the rules get very complex and announcers do get it wrong, but sometimes the officials, including Replay, get it wrong and announcers are obliged to point it out, especially when rules are involved rather than real-time judgments. Judgments are always open for debate, but as I said, today's announcers are very deferential to judgments by officials and almost always extremely fair. If Commissioner Sankey and the SEC believe announcers are treating SEC officiating unfairly, I would suggest reaching out and working with their broadcast partners on rules/officiating would be far more effective than a broadside attack such as this."

That's the actual answer. Announcers rarely attack the officiating, unless they believe it's so egregious that it requires addressing. That's what happened here.

It doesn't mean there's some deep-seated conspiracy on the part of the SEC to protect Texas; these types of missed calls generally even out over time and the crews could have just made a series of mistakes through sheer happenstance. Some Longhorns fans were also up in arms about calls that they believe should have gone against Missouri. But acting like the announcers are the problem, not the refs, is gaslighting.

Sankey does a lot of that, normally when campaigning to get all 16 SEC teams in the 12-team College Football Playoff, but it doesn't make it any less acceptable when it's directed not just at the announcers, but everyone watching too.

item.title: American Airlines plane nearly hit by Air France jet after takeoff at LAX
item.description: Air traffic control audio captured the tense moment an Air France jet made an unauthorized turn into the path of an American Airlines flight at LAX recently. An expert weighed in.
item.content:encoded:
Two passenger jets operated by Air France and American Airlines came dangerously close in the air after departing from Los Angeles International Airport recently.

The incident happened at about 12:20 a.m. on Nov. 7 after the Air France aircraft made a turn it had not been cleared to make, according to a statement the Federal Aviation Administration provided to Fox News Digital.

"The crew of Air France Flight 28 made an unauthorized turn after departing Los Angeles International Airport and went into the path of another aircraft that departed from a parallel runway," the FAA said.

JET PLUNGES 27,000 FEET IN 10 MINUTES AS OXYGEN MASKS SUDDENLY DROP ABOARD FLIGHT

Air traffic control audio captured the tense exchange as controllers worked to redirect the flights.

"Air France 028 heavy, fly heading of 270 immediately," a controller can be heard telling the Air France crew.

Moments later, the controller issued a traffic alert to American Airlines Flight 1660, warning its pilots that another aircraft was directly ahead and less than a mile away.

"Traffic alert, traffic 12 o'clock, less than a mile, maintain 2,000," the controller said.

"OK, we'll go back to 2,000," an American Airlines pilot responded.

Fox News Digital reached out to the two airlines for comment.

"Air France departed from the north side of Los Angeles Airport on a parallel runway from where an American Airlines aircraft took off," Steven Arroyo, an aviation expert and retired airline captain based in Florida, observed to Fox News Digital (he was not connected to the incident). 

"All of a sudden, unannounced, the Air France aircraft made … an unauthorized left-hand turn toward the American Airlines aircraft," he said. 

"They came within 400 feet of each other and less than one mile. That is dangerously close," Arroyo noted.

Once the immediate conflict was addressed, the controller questioned the Air France crew about why the aircraft had turned.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"Air France 028 heavy, you were instructed to climb via SID, not turn to a heading," the controller said.

A SID, or Standard Instrument Departure, is a published departure procedure that can be assigned to an aircraft as part of its flight clearance, according to the FAA's air traffic control procedures.

The controller then asked the Air France crew which departure procedure it had been instructed to follow.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Give me a minute," a pilot responded.

"No problem," the controller said.

The crew later confirmed it had been assigned the SUMMR TWO departure, a published departure procedure from LAX. It was instructed to resume the route, according to the audio.

The FAA said air traffic control immediately issued corrective instructions after the Air France aircraft entered the American Airlines jet's path.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"This was a very dangerous situation and thank goodness, air traffic control was extremely proactive and turned the Air France aircraft heading west before it converged with the American Airlines flight," Arroyo said.

"The FAA will certainly want to take a closer look at this, especially since it's happened several times already here in the past years," he noted.

Arroyo said, however, that "this air traffic controller did an exceptional job."

He also pointed out that such aviation incidents are "very, very rare."

item.title: Dear WNBA media, please stop telling fans to stick to basketball when the drama is what sells
item.description: Chiney Ogwumike asked the media to focus on the basketball, which makes the shooting numbers from Game 7 of the WNBA Finals an awkward place to start.
item.content:encoded:
During a recent episode of OutKick’s "Don’t @ Me with Dan Dakich," Dakich asked me, "What will be the biggest storyline in the WNBA this season, and will it have anything to do with basketball?"

The second part was easy. No.

ANGEL REESE’S WNBA FINALS SHOWED HOW CRITICISM OF HER PLAY BECOMES AN ACCUSATION OF RACISM

And believe me, I care. I just spent over two weeks flying between San Francisco and Atlanta to cover the WNBA Finals. Who won was almost beside the point for me. I was there to ask why both teams were leaving the court before the national anthem and to hear what the players, coaches and the league had to say about it.

In July, ESPN’s Chiney Ogwumike went on "First Take" and called for a reset in how the media covers Caitlin Clark and the WNBA. "In my opinion, we should be giving airtime to the beautiful basketball being played in the 30th year of the WNBA," she said.

As for that beautiful basketball, are you sure that's where you want our attention?

Gabby Williams and Angel Reese entered Game 7 as co-favorites to win WNBA Finals MVP. Through six games, the two had combined to shoot 34.4% from the field. For context, the lowest field goal percentage ever recorded by an NBA Finals MVP was Kobe Bryant's 40.5% in 2010.

At halftime of Game 7, Atlanta led 30–24. That’s 54 points on 31.8% shooting between the two teams. Reese and Williams combined for seven points on 3-for-8 shooting, with five from Reese and two from Williams.

WHY ISN’T ANGEL REESE HELD TO THE CAITLIN CLARK STANDARD WHEN FANS ATTACK HER TEAMMATES?

Then Williams scored 28 points in the second half as Golden State beat Atlanta 68–63 to win its first WNBA championship. She hit the go-ahead three with under three minutes left, finished with 30 points and four blocks, and deserved the trophy. She also shot 32.6% for the series, the lowest field goal percentage by a WNBA Finals MVP.

Reese shot 40.5% from the field in the Finals, including 41.8% in the paint. She missed 28 of her 53 layups. She averaged nearly 13 rebounds, which is one reason you keep her on the floor. You’d still like your 6-foot-4 forward to make a few more shots around the basket.

Is that the basketball that you want us to talk more about, WNBA media?

After Game 3, Reese taunted Golden State with the "too small" gesture, then smiled and waved as the Valkyries walked off the court. She’d just put up 21 points and 12 rebounds, Atlanta was up 2–1, and Reese claimed that she was getting inside the Valkyries’ heads.

She proceeded to shoot 4-for-20 over the next two games and started complaining about the officiating. By Game 6, the player who’d called Golden State too small was one loss from going home.

We’d seen this with Reese before. In the closing moments of the 2023 national championship game, Angel Reese followed Caitlin Clark around the court, taunting her with the "you can’t see me" gesture and pointing to her ring finger. A year later, 12.3 million people watched Clark's Iowa Hawkeyes eliminate Reese's LSU Tigers in the Elite Eight.

This August, Clark’s Fever and Reese’s Dream drew 2.6 million viewers, ESPN’s biggest WNBA audience ever. Clark is the biggest draw in women’s basketball. Put Reese on the other side and you’ve got a rivalry people have been arguing about since they were in college.

The WNBA reported 3.3 million viewers for Game 7. That’s a great number for the league (although it deserves the context that I provided in a recent column). If you tuned in to root against Angel Reese, you still got to watch Gabby Williams take over a championship game.

If you want more people to watch, quit telling them what they’re supposed to care about.

item.title: Nick Foles believes Bears are team to beat in loaded NFC North: 'Something's brewing in Chicago'
item.description: Nick Foles sees something different brewing with the Chicago Bears, pointing to Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson as keys to winning the NFC North.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline has passed, contenders have bolstered their rosters, and now the mad dash to the playoffs truly begins as we head into Week 10.

Looking around the league, the NFC North has cemented itself as the best division in football. If the regular season ended today, all four teams would be in the playoffs, though there can only be one division winner.

Super Bowl-winning quarterback Nick Foles knows all about the battles that occur in the NFC North year after year, and OutKick asked him who he believes will come out on top in the division during a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

He didn’t say so specifically, but one of his former teams during his playing days is standing out right now. They also happen to be atop the division at 7-2.

"There’s something brewing in Chicago, even [Monday] night with, what was it, four interceptions or something? Caleb [Williams’] still slinging it. They’re playing and making plays. [Head coach] Ben Johnson is steady, calm, cool and collected. I think the big thing, too, is if anything happens in the game, watch how he handles the referees. He really doesn’t even mess with them — he’s on to the next one. He’s just locked in, and as players, you look at your head coach and how he responds.

"So, I look at that and say, ‘Man, this team is going to stay locked in. Calm, cool and collected.’"

The Bears are riding high on a four-game win streak, but have barely set themselves apart in the division because the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings are 6-2, followed by a very good Green Bay Packers squad at 6-3.

But Foles sees something in the Bears this season that is different than when he was even there.

"Chicago’s always struggled with an explosive type of offense. They’ve always been a defensive, run-first-type of team. It’s different, man," he said. "Defense is locked in. Dennis Allen is holding it down. Offense is just how many points are they going to score? They can go off at any time, even if you throw four interceptions. They’re still so dangerous."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Foles, though, doesn’t want to discredit the rest of the teams in the division, especially the Vikings with an amazing defensive unit that makes them very scary down the stretch. They also just traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins a day after OutKick interviewed Foles.

"Minnesota Vikings defense, Brian Flores with what he’s doing there — it’s outstanding. Their offense will be their downfall — not doing anything really," Foles said. "I love the Green Bay Packers and how they’re playing right now. And Dan Campbell figuring it out with the Detroit Lions. That tenacity, the offense playing some good ball."

The best part about the NFC North: these teams have to face each other at least one more time. Those will be pivotal division matchups, as all four teams are gunning for a playoff spot.

But as we see in the playoff picture, there is a world where all of them come out of the NFC North and secure a berth to play for the Vince Lombardi Trophy. Only one team will have the home playoff game, though, with a chance to be home throughout the playoffs if things keep tracking.

Foles will get a good look at the Packers specifically during the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game in a couple of weeks on Nov. 25.
